comparison: This current H2 cohort independently executes the full ordinary suite with protocol seed 0, public initialization, named streams and unchanged task/prior/data/sampling laws. Word smoke completes 20001 updates with 23/24 confirmed checks and a recovered passing endpoint, preserving the native transient; its separate 4000-update hold begins at the earliest confirmed checkpoint 834 and passes all 25 checks. Archived final metrics are compared as historical context only, never used to qualify the new cohort. Separate matched H2 performance and width64 fast-path diagnostics retain their own scopes.
conclusion: The single global quintic convolution-rule delta preserves all 19 incumbent BISPF passes across the complete 30-task ordinary suite, with all 11 historical failures retained and no pass regressions. Both ring phases pass every 1200 hold and 300 extension check; actual 3282 updates satisfy the fixed first-convergence stop rule under the maximum 7500-update allowance. All jobs finish without cancellation or retry.

decision_outcomes.reuse_note: Compatible original receipts; overlapping readouts are not independent runs or additive costs

hypothesis: The single global quintic convolution-rule delta preserves every incumbent BISPF pass on the unchanged ordinary task suite while reducing large-image update latency; direct wide-image diagnostics independently test the accelerated path.
next_action: Review the complete same-source performance matrix and direct wide-channel diagnostics together with this preserved full ordinary pass set before selecting one whole BISPF measurement row. Retain all failures, archived controls, exact source identities and unknown performance contention. No public-default adoption or natural-image quality claim follows automatically.

study.competing_explanation: CPU, tiny and dense hosts intentionally retain native updates, so an ordinary suite tie alone cannot establish accelerated large-convolution quality. The separately frozen width-64 tasks test the changed path; held failures, per-task budgets and historical source identities remain visible.
